r15: HL7 defines the syntax and vocabulary for immunization messages and is platform independent. The guide is a joint AIRA/CDC effort with input from NIST, replaces the 2.3.1 guide, is based on HL7 2.5.1, and pre-adopts features of 2.7.1 (data types and the Chapter 2B conformance model).
note: The new guide states the same basis (HL7 2.5.1, platform independent) and says it follows the current HL7 v2 Conformance Methodology, the successor to the 2.7.1 Chapter 2B model. It no longer names 2.7.1 pre-adoption.

r15: Faithful 2.5.1 implementations should be able to accept most messages based on the 2.3.1 guide. Implementations supporting 2.3.1 should continue to follow the 2.3.1 guide (version 2.2, June 2006).
note: The new guide no longer expects 2.3.1 messages to be accepted. It says neither 2.3.1 nor 2.4 is supported nationally, that systems are strongly encouraged to migrate, and that an IIS may require partners to use 2.5.1. It asks systems to keep supporting the previous release of this guide (the 2018 Update).

r15: Two audiences: system managers, who need a high-level understanding, and the technical staff of IIS and EHR-S who implement it. HL7 specifies the interface between two systems, not how either system is implemented.
note: The new guide says it does not prescribe IIS architecture, internal workflows, or business rules.

r15: In scope: sending and receiving immunization histories; requesting histories and evaluated histories with forecasts; responding to those requests; acknowledging receipt; reporting errors; sending observations about an immunization event (funding eligibility, reactions, forecasts, evaluations).
note: The new guide frames scope as two interactions, update (VXU/ACK) and query (QBP/RSP), and names exclusions the 2018 guide did not: ADT, inventory ordering, school and vital records exchange, IIS-to-IIS exchange, IZ Gateway transactions, and federal reporting.

r15: Not in scope: business rules applied when creating or processing a message, a standard transport layer, the search process used to respond to a query, deduplication rules, vaccine inventory, and MPI maintenance. Local implementations are responsible for these.
note: Two of these are now in scope. Transport is required: IIS SHALL implement the CDC WSDL (2015) with a single endpoint for update and query (2.4). Query matching now has requirements on both sides (3.4.5), for example that the IIS SHALL use all submitted patient data to find a match. Deduplication is described (2.3.3) but its rules stay local. Inventory and MPI remain out of scope.

r15: One way to ensure success is to publish a local profile or implementation guide with local business rules. Local guides may further constrain this guide but may not contradict it. This guide identifies key issues that local profiles should address.
note: The new guide says each IIS SHOULD publish a local guide, and adds a section (5.9) with SHALL statements: a local guide that contradicts the national guide SHALL NOT claim conformance and SHALL say where it diverges. It also allows local requirements that differ for policy, legal, or operational reasons, provided they are documented.

r15: Assumptions: infrastructure for accurate, secure exchange is in place; providers reach immunization information through an EHR-S or IIS; privacy and security are implemented; legal and governance issues (access, ownership, data use) are out of scope; the sending system has enough information to build the message; external business rules are documented locally.
note: Not restated as a list. Privacy and security are now partly addressed (transport authentication in 2.4.5, disclosure in 3.5.3); legal and governance issues remain outside the guide.

r15: Systems must be able to accept complete histories from different sources and integrate them, and should not assume any record sent is new; otherwise overlapping histories create duplicates. Points to AIRA's MIROW best practices.
note: 2.3.3 says IIS are built to receive overlapping, repeated, and partial information and reconcile it, and that submitters need not check whether a record already exists. MIROW is cited elsewhere (4.6.4.3, 4.6.5.1).

r15: Chapter-by-chapter outline; boxed notes mark changes from the 2.3.1 guide. "The focus of this guide is on the format and grammar of the messages between systems."
note: The new guide is organized differently (narrative chapters 1-6, then the computable Message Infrastructure in chapter 7) and is no longer limited to format and grammar: chapter 4 gives topic guidance on data, and narrative requirements are stated to be as binding as the machine-testable ones.

r15: Primary actors are the IIS and EHR-S (and other systems); supporting actors are an MPI and an HIE. Sender is the initiator of a conversation. Table 2-1 lists each actor's responsibilities and messaging goals. Actors can be decomposed into roles: immunization history supplier, consumer, and identity resolution broker.
note: The new guide uses two roles, submitting system and querying system, with the IIS as receiver and responder. The MPI actor and identity-broker role are gone. HIEs remain, now with a requirement: an intermediary must be transparent and the final response must come from the IIS.

r15: Use cases are mapped from the actor goals (Figure 1). Identity resolution may be separate from the history request or implicit in it. An "IIS AO" is an organization authorized to submit to and request from an IIS.
note: The new guide covers identity resolution implicitly, through the query and candidate-selection flow (3.4.6).

r15: Send an immunization history for a client from one system to another (VXU Z22). Other systems, such as vital records or billing, could use it. Post-condition: the receiver has accepted the history.
note: The new guide limits scope to IIS update and query; vital records exchange is excluded.

section: Use Cases 2 and 3 - Request Complete History; Request Evaluated History and Forecast
r15: Request a complete history (QBP Z34 / RSP Z32) or an evaluated history and forecast (QBP Z44 / RSP Z42). Five possible results: one exact match, one or more inexact matches, no match, a match whose data the client asked not to share, errors. The definition of "exact" is a local business rule and should be documented. Systems must handle clients whose records are protected, and should document it.
guide: query-by-parameter-qbp-message-profiles unified-z34-and-z44-profile-model rsp-response-profiles z31-return-a-list-of-candidates z33-return-a-response-with-no-person-records patient-matching-responsibilities selecting-a-candidate-match information-disclosure-constraints
note: The same outcomes map to Z32/Z42, Z31, and Z33. The new guide adds detail: Z31 normally lists two or three candidates, and when there are too many the IIS returns QAK-2 TM rather than a long list; a protected record is returned as Z33; matching requirements apply to both sides (3.4.5); disclosure is limited to what confirms the match (3.5.3). Z34 and Z44 now share one model.

r15: Send demographic data, as an update or a new record. Demographic-only data may be sent in a VXU (Z22) or in ADT messages; ADT profiles are not in this guide.
note: New requirement: IIS SHALL accept VXUs with demographic information whether or not they contain immunizations. Submitters SHALL coordinate before sending demographic-only VXUs routinely, and SHOULD use ADT for routine demographic updates. ADT remains out of scope.

section: Use Cases 5 and 6 - Acknowledge Receipt; Report Error
r15: Acknowledge receipt of a message, indicating success or failure, possibly with errors (ACK Z23, RSP Z33). A well-formed query that finds no candidates is reported in the acknowledgement. Errors may reject the message or parts of it.
note: The ACK is now defined in terms of core intent (whether the patient and vaccinations were recorded), with severity and follow-up rules (3.3). Detailed ACK guidance is compared under chapter 6 and Appendix B.

section: Messaging in the Context of the Business Process
r15: Steps for the sender (assemble data, build, connect, send) and receiver (check format, parse, evaluate, acknowledge, deduplicate client and events, insert or update). Partners must agree on how to connect. Parts of a message may have errors that are not sufficient to reject it. Business rules for sender and receiver should be clearly specified. Which client's record to send is outside the guide.
note: The new guide describes the clinical workflow rather than the processing steps. Partial acceptance survives as core intent: a message is accepted when the patient and vaccinations can be recorded, even with field-level errors.

section: Messaging in the Context of the Business Process (note)
r15: Each implementation should document its business rules in a local guide or profile. Local implementers may further constrain this guide: optional or RE elements may be made required, and repeating fields may be limited to fewer repetitions.
note: The new guide still allows constraint, but discourages tightening RE to R to express program policy (5.10): use R only when the IIS cannot accept the record without the data, and enforce RE handling instead of reclassifying.

section: Core Data Elements of an Immunization History
r15: Lists IIS responsibilities (consolidation, supplying histories, forecasting, evaluation, inventory, funding reports, coverage, privacy, reminders, lot recall tracking). The NVAC core data elements determine usage in this guide; systems using it are expected to support them and include them in messages; they also appear in conformance statements. Sending forecasts is required of systems that output CDS results; consuming them is required of systems that request them.
note: The reference is now the CDC Core Data Elements for Functional Standards, used as a catalog of definitions, not as the basis for usage. The new guide adds a conceptual data model (patient, guardian, vaccination).

section: Pre-Adoption of Some Features of HL7 Version 2.7.1
r15: Pre-adopts 2.7.1 conformance statements, conditional predicates, usage guidance, and new MSH fields.
note: These are features of the profiles; the new guide follows the HL7 v2 Conformance Methodology.

r15: Specific vocabularies (LOINC, SNOMED) are called for. It is best practice to use the most current version of the coding system.
note: The new guide adds requirements for keeping dynamic code sets current (4.3.1) and CVX timeliness (4.6.2.2.5).

r15: Receiving systems expect complete histories (all immunization information known to the sender) and do not process in snapshot mode (incoming data does not replace existing data). Receiving systems are responsible for publishing the consolidation rules they apply.
note: The 2018 addendum (Appendix C, Processing Mode Clarification, r15-c-05) already reversed the first part: a VXU may carry only the changed vaccinations. The new guide follows the addendum (one VXU per vaccination or per encounter) and implies no snapshot processing (2.3.3: IIS consolidate rather than preserve submissions), but does not say that a VXU never replaces the existing record, nor that IIS should publish their consolidation rules.
recommendation: Consider one sentence in 2.3.3: "A VXU adds to and updates the IIS record; it does not replace it (no snapshot processing). IIS SHOULD document the consolidation rules they apply."

r15: The guide defines constrainable profiles, identified in MSH-21.
note: MSH-21 is defined in the profiles.

r15: Assumes access to the HL7 2.5.1 standard; uses 2.7.1 Chapter 2B rules; data types are described separately; no conformance information is given for optional elements; X is used sparingly (for B and W elements, and some conditional elements); without an agreed profile a sender need not send, and a receiver need not process, O elements.
note: Usage conventions are in the profiles. The new guide explains usage in operational terms (2.9) and documents where it departs from the base standard (5.11).

r15: MUST/SHALL/REQUIRED, MUST NOT/SHALL NOT, SHOULD/RECOMMENDED, SHOULD NOT/NOT RECOMMENDED, and MAY/OPTIONAL defined (RFC 2119 style). MAY items cannot be expected without agreement between partners; implementations with and without an optional element MUST interoperate.
note: The new guide uses SHALL, SHALL NOT, SHOULD, SHOULD NOT, and MAY (not MUST or REQUIRED), and adds that requirements on system behavior that cannot be tested in a message are equally normative.

r15: Definitions of message, segment group, segment, field, and component, with examples.

A null value ("") differs from an empty field: an empty field should not overwrite data in the receiving system, while "" means the previous value should be cleared. Null fields should not be sent in immunization messages. Systems that send "", or that accept and process it, must say so in their local implementation guides.
note: Neither the narrative nor the profiles say what "" means or whether it may be sent. The 2018 code tables (PD1-12) rely on the distinction too. This affects updates: a receiver that treats "" as a value, or an empty field as "clear", will corrupt records.
recommendation: Restore the rule, for example in 4.6.4 (Updates and Deletes) or 2.9: "An empty field means no change. Systems SHOULD NOT send the HL7 null value (""); systems that send or act on it SHALL document this in their local guide."

r15: Data types restrict field contents; code sets and value sets are maintained by standards organizations.
Applications must use agreed delimiters. Messages SHALL use <CR> as segment terminator and | ^ & ~ \ as field, component, subcomponent, repetition, and escape characters.
note: MSH-1 and MSH-2 are fixed in the profiles; 2.4.4 covers line terminators within the SOAP payload.

r15: Abstract message syntax ({} repeat, [] optional; nested groups).
Users of the guide agreed to eliminate Z segments so that immunization data are sent the same way nationally. The query name code beginning with Z is not a Z segment.
note: The profiles allow no Z segments, so a Z segment fails validation; the narrative no longer states the agreement. Low impact.

section: Basic Message Processing Rules - Message Acknowledgement
r15: Original mode processing only; enhanced mode is not supported. Each message (VXU, QBP) gets one response (ACK, RSP); the ACK is not itself acknowledged. Only application acknowledgements are in scope.
note: The new guide keeps one application-level ACK per VXU and adds that an ACK never reports transport faults. It changes the acknowledgement fields: MSH-15/MSH-16 now take NE (see conformance statement IZ-42 above), and an intermediary relaying an IIS transport problem should use the enhanced-mode code CR rather than AR.

section: Basic Message Processing Rules - Message Acknowledgement
r15: ACKs alert the sender to errors and to data that did not reach the receiver. An intermediary such as an HIE should pass the ACK back to the sending system.
note: The new guide requires the final response to be generated by the IIS and to reflect the true disposition, with the intermediary transparent to the submitter.

r15: Nine encoding rules: segment order, segment ID first, field separators, trailing empty components need not be sent, leading empty components must be, length applies to each repetition, trailing field separators are not an error.
note: The profiles and the HL7 base standard govern encoding; NIST's validator applies them.

r15: Receiving rules that cascade: extra fields are ignored; a field with bad data is treated as empty (error, continue); an empty required field makes the segment empty; an out-of-order segment is treated as empty; an empty required segment in a group empties the group; an empty required segment outside a group, or an empty required group, rejects the message. Optional or unexpected segments are ignored. All errors should be reported to the sender.
note: Acceptance is now decided by core intent: a VXU is rejected only when the patient cannot be associated or created or Critical Data cannot be stored. IIS SHALL NOT return severity E for conformance violations alone (for example, segment mis-ordering) unless they prevent core intent. Errors are still reported in ERR segments. The cascade (field to segment to group to message) is not described.

section: Determining Usage of Segments, Fields and Components
r15: Rules used to set usage: elements required by HL7 are R or RE; NVAC core data elements are R or RE and their segments RE; backward-compatibility (B) elements SHALL be unsupported (X); conditional elements stay C unless that conflicts; everything else is O.
note: The new guide sets usage by how IIS actually operate, and relaxes base-standard requirements where they do not serve IIS workflows, documenting each divergence (5.11). The resulting usage changes are listed in the tables above.

section: Usage Conformance Testing Recommendations; Sending and Receiving Application Conformance (Tables 3-2)
r15: Usage codes cited from HL7 2.7.1 Chapter 2B, separately for sender and receiver. R: sender SHALL populate; receiver SHALL process it and SHALL raise an exception when it is absent. RE: sender SHALL populate when relevant data exist; receiver SHALL process the message when it is omitted. X: sender SHALL NOT populate; receiver SHALL ignore it and MAY raise an exception. O: not yet defined (to be profiled). Footnote on the two interpretations of RE.
note: 2.9.1 gives one interpretation for both parties. R: a missing or unusable element SHALL be reported with an ERR (not necessarily a rejection). RE: the receiver may report the omission. O: if sent, the receiver processes it (the 2018 guide said a receiver need not process O without agreement). X: the receiver does not process, store, or use it. 2.6.1 settles the RE interpretation question.

r15: C(a/b) resolves to usage a when the predicate is true and b when false; C(X/X) is used where the element the condition depends on is X. No predicate is given for C(O/X).
note: Predicates are in the profiles; changed conditions are listed in the tables above.

r15: Local implementations may constrain this guide and should mark elements the local application ignores as IX (if sent, it is ignored).
note: 2.9.1 defines IX the same way, as a convention for local guides, and adds that sending an IX element is not an error.

r15: Columns of the message, segment, and data type tables (SEQ, usage, cardinality, value set, and so on).

Z22 sends an immunization history, new or updated, from an EHR-S, IIS, or other system; its partner is Z23. The trigger may be a new or updated record. The message may pass through intermediaries such as an HIE; the acknowledgement MUST be returned to the initiating system.
note: Same purpose. The new guide adds when a VXU is expected (3.2.5 submission scenarios) and that the IIS generates the final response through any intermediary.

section: 5. Profile Z22 - Dynamic Definition; 6. Profile Z23 - Dynamic Definition
r15: AR is returned when the message type, event, or processing ID is unsupported, or the message cannot be processed for reasons unrelated to format or content. Otherwise AA when there are no errors and AE when there are errors; if the errors are fatal the message is rejected (still AE), otherwise the data are integrated.
note: MSA-1 is now derived from the most severe ERR-4: AR SHALL be returned when the VXU is rejected (any severity E, core intent not fulfilled); AE means accepted with warnings; AA means accepted with no issues needing correction. A rejected message is no longer reported as AE. Systems that read AE as "some data rejected" need to change. (This follows the ACK TAB of June 2026.)

r15: A VXU may be new to the receiver or an update to an existing record. Segment table, with comments such as "not described in this guide, may be locally specified" for SFT, PV1/PV2, GT1, IN2/IN3, TQ1/TQ2.
note: Segment usage and cardinality are compared in Message structure above.

r15: Z23 acknowledges receipt and processing of a VXU or QBP. Through an intermediary, the acknowledgement MUST be returned to the initiating system. The ACK may report errors (ERR, included if there are errors).
note: The new ACK profile is largely new material (core intent, severity, ERR-5 national codes, follow-up actions, monitoring), adopted from the ACK TAB. ERR segments may now appear in an accepted message.

r15: Z34 requests a complete immunization history: demographics, immunizations received, and patient conditions that affect immunization (allergies, contraindications, history of vaccine-preventable disease). The response is very similar to a VXU.
note: The new guide defines the complete history as all immunizations known to the IIS; patient observations (contraindications, immunity) are covered in 4.4.4.4 and 4.8.

r15: Query parameters may include demographic and address data; no sorting. The guide does not specify the matching logic; parameters may feed a simple or probabilistic search. The search method should be specified locally.
note: Matching is still local, but the new guide sets expectations: the querying system SHALL send all known identifying information; the IIS SHALL use all of it and SHOULD use probabilistic or other advanced matching (3.4.5); the IIS SHALL NOT return a record on a single identifier (3.4.7). QBP is used only for immediate responses.

section: 7. Z34 Response Characteristics; Response to Different Outcomes (Table 7-2)
r15: No match: Z33. One high-confidence match: Z32. One or more lower-confidence matches up to the maximum: Z31 "if state law allows" (more than one high-confidence match counts as lower confidence). More than the maximum (the lower of the requested and the IIS limit): Z33, too many matches. One match that does not allow sharing: Z33 "no candidates found". Not well formed with fatal errors: Z33. Unsupported message type, event, or processing ID: ACK with errors. Not identifiable as HL7: no response. The definition of a match is local and should be documented.
note: The outcomes largely carry over (Z32, Z31, Z33 for no match, too many, or not shareable). The change: a query that is malformed or fails before matching (bad MSH or QPD) now gets a Z23 ACK, not a Z33; Z33 means the query was processed but no record can be returned. The new guide also says a Z31 normally holds two or three candidates and the IIS returns SR identifiers for selection. Whether a protected record is reported as "not found" or as "exists but not shareable" is not stated.

r15: The querying system sends a QBP; the responding system returns one response (sequence and activity diagrams).
note: IIS SHALL respond to each valid QBP with exactly one RSP.

r15: Z32 returns a complete immunization history in response to Z34, to support transferring a person's record between systems; similar to a VXU in content.
note: The new guide adds that returned demographics are for confirming the match, not for updating local patient records (3.5.3).

r15: Z31 returns a complete list of candidate patients so the requester can re-query on the selected candidate. It is a response to Z34.
note: Z31 may now answer a Z44 as well as a Z34. The new guide adds rules for the re-query: it SHALL use all the identifying information returned for the selected candidate (including the SR), and the selection SHALL NOT become a permanent link without the user's awareness.

r15: Z33 returns an acknowledgement with no person records when (1) an error occurred processing the query, (2) no high-confidence match was found, including a match that may not be shared or an IIS that does not support Z31, or (3) too many matches were found.
note: Cases 2 and 3 carry over (too many matches is QAK-2 TM). Case 1 moves: a query that cannot be processed because the message itself is malformed now gets a Z23.

r15: Z44 requests an evaluated history and forecast: limited demographics, the immunization history validated by a CDS engine, and a forecast of next doses due.
note: Z34 and Z44 are unified: both return the complete history; Z44 SHALL also include evaluation and recommendations, and Z34 MAY include them. Querying systems should ignore evaluation and forecast content they do not need.

section: 11. Z44 Response Characteristics; Response Grammar to Different Outcomes (Tables 11-2, 11-3)
r15: No match: Z33. One high-confidence match: Z42. One or more lower-confidence matches: Z33, "no matches", and no records returned (no candidate list for Z44). Malformed with fatal errors: Z33. Unsupported message type, event, or processing ID: ACK with errors. Not identifiable as HL7: no response.
note: A Z44 may now receive a Z31 candidate list, as Z34 does. A malformed query gets a Z23.

section: 11. Z44 Query Profile (note on protected records)
r15: Each system determines how to handle patients who want their records protected: treat them as not in the system, or respond that the person exists but does not allow sharing. The rule should be documented in the local profile.
note: The new guide returns a Z33 when a record cannot be disclosed, and covers consent models in 4.5.6, but does not say whether the response may reveal that a protected record exists, or that the choice should be documented locally.
recommendation: Add to 3.5.2.4 whether a Z33 for a protected record may differ from "not found" (QAK-2, ERR), and that the IIS SHOULD document its choice in its local guide.

r15: Z42 returns an evaluated history and forecast. It is not intended to support transfer of the complete immunization history.
note: Z42 now returns the complete immunization history along with evaluation and forecast.

section: 13. Batch File Specifications - Sending Messages in a Batch
r15: Systems may send messages in batches (BHS ... BTS), and batches in files (FHS ... FTS); a single batch needs no FHS/FTS, and a stream of messages needs neither. BHS/FHS field tables, with IZ-8/IZ-9 fixing the separators.
note: HL7 batch files are no longer described, and NIST's profiles did not include them. The new guide's only batch rule is transport: the CDC WSDL has no batch protocol, so batch processing SHALL be sequential submitSingleMessage requests. Files of batched VXUs (still used for some flat-file or SFTP uploads) are not covered.
recommendation: Say explicitly whether FHS/BHS batch files remain a permitted local option (outside this guide) or are retired.

section: Core Data Elements for an Immunization History (Table B-2)
r15: The NVAC core data elements, with a support status (must be supported and sent if known): client ID, name, mother's maiden name, race, ethnicity, sex, birth date, birth order, birth state, birth facility, address, phone, IIS and provider status (PD1-16), responsible person name and relationship, vaccine product, manufacturer, date, lot, expiration date, site, route, ordering and administering provider, information source, VIS type and dates, eligibility, contraindications with dates, refusal reason and date, history of disease with date. Optional: multiple birth indicator, responsible person address and phone, language, funding source, reactions.
note: The new guide refers to the CDC Core Data Elements for Functional Standards instead, and some CDEs are Critical Data for acceptance (3.3.1). Its conceptual data model leaves out birth state, birth facility, birth order, and mother's maiden name, which the 2018 list required support for. Field-level support is in the profiles.

r15: Illustrative process; local rules must be documented. The receiver validates against HL7 and local rules and looks for the client. No match: add the client. One match with protection indicator Y: do not integrate the record, and acknowledge without revealing that the client exists. One match otherwise: integrate by local rules. More than one match: local rules (pending, reject, or load as new for later cleanup).
note: Acceptance is defined by core intent (patient associated or created). The new guide does not tell the IIS to refuse to integrate a protected patient's VXU: in opt-out jurisdictions submitters SHALL send all records and the IIS enforces consent after receipt. Ambiguous matches may be queued for manual review (2.3.3).

r15: A sending system may say it does not accept acknowledgements, in which case none is returned; this is not recommended. The sender's handling of the ACK is local; good practice is to alert the user and support troubleshooting.
note: An IIS SHALL return exactly one ACK for each VXU received, and the profiles now fix MSH-15/MSH-16 to NE, so a sender can no longer opt out. The new guide adds requirements on submitters for following up on ACK severities (3.3.3.3) and monitoring (3.3.5).

r15: Conformant systems should populate and process R and RE elements, conditional elements when the predicate is met, and handle repeating elements gracefully.

Eligibility (which program should pay) differs from funding source (which program did pay). Eligibility is recorded for each dose administered, not needed for historical doses. Systems capturing eligibility per visit associate it with each dose given at that visit, considering whether the vaccine is eligible. OBX-17 records the capture method (VXC40 per immunization, VXC41 per visit). Refers to MIROW.
note: Same model, now with SHALL statements (per-dose capture, at most one eligibility per dose). Funding source gains its own section with two- and three-stock models (4.6.5.2). New: IIS SHALL NOT return eligibility or funding source in RSP messages.

section: Example VXU #2 - Technical Note; Eligibility Outcomes (Table B-2)
r15: Interfaces and validation should ensure the patient eligibility matches the vaccine's eligibility (same funding program). Only one eligibility applies to a dose. A VFC-eligible patient receiving a vaccine that is not VFC eligible is recorded as V01.
note: The new guide puts what happened first: IIS SHALL accept eligibility and funding combinations that are possible in practice, even when they break program policy, and SHOULD use data quality follow-up rather than conformance rules (unless the jurisdiction chooses stricter enforcement). The V01 rule for non-VFC vaccines is not stated.

r15: Local programs are published in the local guide's table 0064. V07 may be used for a person eligible for a state or local program but not VFC; local codes may be preferable. A local code is the HL70363 assigning authority code plus a two-digit number (for example AKA01, with AKA as the coding system); a local code implies the person is not VFC eligible.
note: Local codes now follow a jurisdiction pattern such as AK01 with an assigning authority, SHALL be published, and SHALL NOT duplicate national concepts. V07 and the "local code implies not VFC eligible" rule are not mentioned.

section: Example VXU #4 - Send client specific conditions
r15: Factors affecting evaluation and forecast are sent in OBX segments: reactions to a previous dose (even when the dose is unknown), evidence of immunity (serology is strongest; a clinician-determined history of disease), contraindications (temporary or permanent: allergies, conditions, medications, illness), and risk factors or exposures (for example rabies) that call for a vaccine.
note: Section 4.8 covers each concept with storage and response rules, for example IIS SHALL NOT reject a message because immunity information is included, and SHOULD say (severity I) when reactions are not stored.

section: Example VXU #6 - Delete an Immunization Record
r15: Each system may have rules about who may delete. If deletion by HL7 is allowed, use RXA-21. The sender's ID for the immunization goes in ORC-3 with its assigning authority; the receiver must store these to match a later delete.
note: Deletion is no longer optional for the IIS: it SHALL support deletes of records the submitter reported. Submitters SHOULD NOT delete another source's records, SHALL reuse ORC-3, and a delete SHALL carry the identifying values previously sent. A delete retracts the source record, not necessarily the consolidated event.

section: VXU Example #7 - Send Information About Vaccine Information Statement (VIS)
r15: VIS type, edition date, and date presented are sent in OBX segments linked by OBX-4. The 2D barcode fully-encoded text string (24 digits, not the 13-digit GDTI) is highly recommended and implies the edition date. The vaccine-type method (CVX plus edition date) is problematic and "anticipated to be retired in a future release".
note: The vaccine-type method is not retired: IIS SHALL support both methods and submitters SHALL support at least one (the barcode method is still preferred; the alternate uses an unspecified-formulation CVX). New rules: accept unrecognized barcodes and unexpected dates, date given not after administration, multiple VIS per vaccine, and never reject a vaccination for VIS problems.

section: VXU Example #8 - Send Information Indicating Immunization Refusal
r15: A refusal is sent with the reason in RXA-18, completion status RE in RXA-20, and amount 0. The ORC is still required; the filler order number is required but meaningless. RXA-2 is not a dose number (constrained to 1).
note: The new guide defines a refusal narrowly (vaccine due and declined; not missed appointments, shortages, or contraindications), sets ORC-3 to 9999, and allows a refusal-only VXU.

section: VXU Example #9 - Send Two Lot Numbers in RXA
r15: When components are packaged together with linked lot numbers (for example Pentacel), send only the first component's lot in RXA-15. When an adjuvant is added at administration and its lot is not linked, record it as a separate order group (ORC/RXA).
note: The new guide only says to report the NDC of the lyophilized powder rather than the diluent. Which lot to send for kits, and how to record a separately added adjuvant, are not covered.
recommendation: Add a short rule on lot numbers for kits and separately added components, in 4.6.2.3 or the RXA-15 notes.

r15: Birth information supports identity resolution: birth registration number as a PID-3 identifier (type BR), birth order PID-24, multiple birth indicator PID-25, birth state as a PID-11 address with type BDL, birth facility PID-23 (not used for birth state).
note: The fields remain in the profiles, but the narrative no longer explains how to send birth state (BDL address) or birth facility, or their value for matching.

section: VXU Example #11 - Recording an incompletely administered dose or a non-potent dose
r15: A partially administered dose (for example the child pulled away) is recorded with RXA-20 = PA, to support inventory and recall; details may go in an NTE under an OBX.
note: The new guide names PA as a finalized outcome but does not say why to report it or how to add detail.

section: Send Acknowledgement ACK In Response To VXU
r15: ACKs let senders troubleshoot and learn what did not reach the receiver; an intermediary must pass the ACK back. Errors may come from HL7 violations, local rule violations, transport failures, or authentication failures; only the first two are addressed by the guide.
note: Transport and authentication failures are now in scope, reported as SOAP faults (2.4.3), and SHALL NOT be reported in an ACK.

r15: AR is reserved for four errors (unsupported message type, event, processing ID; unable to process for reasons unrelated to format or content), for example an unrecognized version. HL7 errors that reject the message (empty required group, missing PID or MSH) or local rule violations that reject it (birth date in the future) are AE with severity E. An invalid RXA-5 rejects that order group; an empty NK1-3 rejects only the NK1; data in an X field (PID-2) is a warning and is ignored. ERR-8 text is generated locally.
note: A rejected message is now AR, never AE. Severity E is only for core intent not fulfilled, so an invalid vaccine code in one order group is reported per issue rather than by cascading rejection. ERR-5 uses the national error codes, and ERR-8 has its own guidance (3.3.3.6).

section: Example Return an Evaluated History and Forecast (RSP Z42)
r15: The guide does not specify the function or accuracy of forecasting; implementations should document local specifics. It is not meant to support calling a forecasting service, only messaging forecasts as part of a history. Evaluation is against a schedule; schedules define series by vaccine group.
note: The new guide anchors series definitions to CDSi and requires a recommendation for every standard age-based series (4.7.2, 4.7.5). Clinical content stays with the jurisdiction.

section: Codes Supporting Messaging Evaluation and Forecasting (Table B-3)
r15: Data elements and LOINC codes: schedule (59779-9, required), vaccine group (30956-7 preferred; 38890-0 for backward compatibility), series name, dose number, dose validity, number of doses (adjusted for skipped doses), series status, earliest/recommended/latest/overdue dates, recommendation reason (local codes).
note: The codes are bound in the OBX co-constraints (format). What is required changes: schedule, series name, and dose counts are now optional (MAY); series status SHALL be returned for every forecast; earliest and recommended dates SHALL be returned when another dose is due; dose validity is Y or N. A forecast SHALL start with 30956-7, and 38890-0 SHALL NOT be used for that (2018 allowed it for backward compatibility). This follows the CDS in RSP TAB.

r15: Evaluation follows the administered RXA; recommendations follow an RXA for CVX 998 (no vaccine administered), not existing RXAs. Each observation is its own OBX, linked to its vaccine group by OBX-4; OBX order is not regulated. Combination vaccines get one set of observations per vaccine group. Multiple recommendations go under a single ORC/RXA with sets of OBX grouped by sub-ID.
note: The new guide requires exactly one forecast order group after all history and non-administration groups, and a forecast for every standard age-based series.

section: Indicating the Schedule that was used
r15: Schedule is required when evaluation or recommendation is sent. The only schedule CDC supports is ACIP; systems may define local schedules.
note: The schedule observation is now optional (MAY), with the caution that it is not consistently standardized.

section: Reporting Next Dose Recommendation Dates; Recommendation Reasons
r15: Definitions of earliest (no grace period), recommended, overdue (locally defined), and latest dates; not all apply. Recommendation reasons are local codes, documented locally.
note: The new guide adds that each reason is a separate OBX.

section: Important notes; Using the NTE segment
r15: OBX set IDs increase through the message; sub-IDs are unique within an order group; a VIS OBX gets its own sub-ID. An NTE under an OBX may carry notes the receiver may display; any use is local and documented locally.
note: OBX-1 and OBX-4 rules are in 4.4.2 and the profiles (format). NTE is not mentioned anywhere in the new narrative.

section: Issues Outside of Messaging That Impact the Value Sent
r15: Skipped doses (for example Hib catch-up) should be handled in local profiles; booster doses do not add to the primary series count; prior infection is messaged as immunity.

section: Send Request for Complete Immunization History - protected clients
r15: When a client who does not want data shared is found, local rules apply: respond as "no records found", except that the provider who set the protection may get the record; or return limited information saying the person exists but is protected.
note: The new guide returns Z33 when consent prevents disclosure. The exception for the provider who set the protection, and the option of acknowledging that the record exists, are not addressed. See also r15-11-03.

section: Send Request for Complete Immunization History - handling the response
r15: The requesting system decides locally how users review a returned history or candidate list: accept, reject, mark for review, select a candidate and send a new QBP with the identifying information from the RSP, or refine the query.
All QPD fields are RE: senders may populate any or all; receivers must accept values in any of them but may specify which are required and which they ignore.
note: Querying systems SHALL send all known identifying information (including the SR when known), and the IIS SHALL use all of it.

section: Returning a list of candidate clients
r15: A candidate list returns all known information for each candidate in PID, NK1, and PD1, with PID-1 numbering each candidate. If there are more candidates than the requested or allowed maximum, an error acknowledgement is sent. The matching logic is not specified.
note: Disclosure is now minimized: return what lets the user confirm the match, not everything known (3.5.3). Each candidate carries the IIS identifier (SR) for the follow-up query.

r15: The response returned the querying system's medical record number and the IIS identifier.
note: Now a requirement, with a condition: the submitter's identifier is returned only when the IIS has associated it with the record, and other submitters' identifiers SHOULD NOT be returned.

section: Acknowledging a query that finds no candidates; finds more candidates than requested
r15: No match is not an error; respond with Z33 and QAK-2 NF. RCP-2 sets the requester's limit; the responder's own limit, if lower, wins; too many gives Z33 with QAK-2 TM.

section: Using a Two-step process to request an immunization history
r15: Alternative identity resolution through an MPI using IHE PIX (ITI-8, ITI-30 Pediatric Demographics option) and PDQ, then a QBP with the retrieved identifier.
note: MPI interactions and IHE profiles are not mentioned; the new guide's scope is IIS update and query only.

section: Receiving system determines that message has errors
r15: A well-formed query with a content error (QPD-2 query tag missing) gets a Z33 with errors (QAK-1 empty). A message of unrecognized type gets an ACK with AR.
note: A query rejected for a problem in MSH or QPD now gets a Z23 ACK rather than a Z33.

r15: Lists AIRA guidance not binding on Release 1.5 but expected to be required in future releases: ACK guidance, the national set of error codes, RSP guidance, detailed message structure and LOINC use, and the query/response functional guide.
note: These are now built into the guide, much of it through the TABs (ACK, CDS in RSP); the TAB comparison pages show how completely.

section: Coding Systems and Value Sets (from Addendum)
r15: A coding system differs from a value set; CE.3/CWE.3 should name the coding system (HL70396), not the value set. Table of the expected coding system for each coded field.
note: Coding systems are bound in the profiles; changes are in the tables above.

r15: "Repetition" means occurrence: the first repetition is the first occurrence.

Responses are synchronous: the sender waits for the response before sending the next message (parallel processes allowed); RCP-2 = I. Z22, Z34, Z44 use MSH-15 ER and MSH-16 AL: a message failing initial validation (type, version, processing ID) gets a Z23 ACK; one that passes gets the application response. One response per message.
note: Synchronous exchange and one response per message carry over (QBP is used only for immediate responses). MSH-15 and MSH-16 change from ER/AL to NE/NE (conformance statement IZ-42 above). The rule that waiting for a response is required before sending the next message is not stated.

r15: Z22 may carry only the vaccinations added, updated, or deleted, not the whole history; the receiver should not assume a VXU is the entire history. Each order group should hold the complete data about that vaccination. Z32 carries the whole history; the receiver may overwrite or reconcile. Z42 carries all immunizations evaluated and a complete forecast, but not every detail (for example lot number); use Z34/Z32 for a complete history.
note: The VXU part carries over (one VXU per vaccination or per encounter; updates for changed fields). Z42 changes: it now returns the complete history, so it is no longer a reduced view. The rule that each order group carries the complete data for its vaccination is only implied.

r15: To delete a record, resend the most recent message for it unchanged except for the action code D (RXA-21), with the same ORC-3; then send any corrected records as new messages.
For a refusal or deferral, RXA-3 is the date the refusal or deferral was recorded. For a forecast dose, it is the date the forecast was made.
note: For a refusal, RXA-3 is now the date the vaccination would have been given if accepted (usually the same day, but not the date of data entry). When the RXA only carries a condition (RXA-20 NA), its dates carry no meaning and the IIS should not act on them. The forecast rule is kept: RXA-3 is when the evaluation and forecast were done.

r15: CVX is strongly preferred and required for vaccines; a local guide may allow NDC or CPT instead. The second triplet may carry the same vaccine in another code system, where NDC is preferred.
note: NDC is now a full alternative, not a local option: an IIS SHALL accept an administered dose reported with only an NDC, and SHALL check that CVX and NDC agree when both are sent. CPT stays a local option (MAY).

section: RXA-6 Administered Amount; RXA-7 Administered Units
r15: When the administered amount is unknown, send 999 in RXA-6 (and then no units). The preferred unit for RXA-7 is mL.
note: The profiles keep 999 (required for refusals and CVX 998, and RXA-7 is X when RXA-6 is 999), but neither the profiles nor the narrative say to use 999 when the amount of a given dose is unknown, for example on a historical record. The preferred unit is not mentioned.
recommendation: Add a sentence to 3.2.4.2 or 4.6.1.2: when the dose volume is unknown, RXA-6 is 999 and RXA-7 is empty; otherwise the volume is given in mL.

r15: The primary use is the information source (administered or historical, NIP001), which all systems should support; IIS rely on it. Other notes may follow in later repetitions if specified locally, with the first repetition empty when no information source is sent; text-only notes are by local agreement.
note: Inbound, the meaning is the same and is now an identifying field: changing it requires a delete and an add. In responses, the IIS SHOULD NOT distinguish administered from historical and querying systems SHOULD ignore the indicator. The use of later repetitions for other notes is not mentioned.

r15: The name and address of the facility that gave the vaccine: component 4 is the facility identifier (an OID in the universal ID if populated, not a local code; systems may publish a table of local values), and components 9-15 are the facility address.
note: RXA-11 now identifies the administering organization, not a place: an IIS-assigned identifier in RXA-11.4, and the IIS SHOULD NOT read it as an address. The OID and the address components are not mentioned. RXA-11.4 is also an identifying field, and RXA-11 SHOULD be empty for historical doses.

r15: If RXA-21 is empty, no action is indicated. Most IIS decide between add and update by their own criteria, so it is common practice to send A even for a vaccination reported before; do not assume updates will be marked U.
note: Submitters SHALL now support A, U, and D and SHALL send U when only non-identifying fields change (identifying changes are a delete and an add). The IIS side is unchanged: it SHALL match at the vaccination level whether a record comes as A or U. Updates are also limited to real changes.

section: MSH-4 Sending Facility; MSH-22 and MSH-23 Responsible Organizations
r15: MSH-4 is the organization responsible for operating the sending application; its first component is the namespace ID from table 0362 and the second and third are reserved for OIDs. MSH-22 is the business organization accountable for the content (needed when organizations share a service bureau); MSH-23 is the organization legally responsible for acting on it.
note: Section 2.7 keeps the meanings and goes further: MSH-4 SHALL match the authenticated connection, MSH-22 may be empty when it is the same organization, and all organization fields use an IIS-defined identifier in HD.1 (OIDs remain optional). MSH-23 is not discussed.

r15: MSH-3 and MSH-5 name the specific instance, not the product (for example GRITS, not WIR), with locally assigned codes. MSH-10 is unique within the sending facility, application, and day of MSH-7, and is echoed in MSA. If MSH-17 is empty, assume USA.
note: The new narrative does not discuss these fields; the profiles carry only their format. None is likely to cause interoperability problems, but the MSH-10 uniqueness scope is what receivers rely on to detect resent messages.
recommendation: Consider a short MSH paragraph in 2.7 or 3.3 covering MSH-3/5 instance names and MSH-10 uniqueness.

r15: IN1 is specified because several IIS require it; local guides that need it should base requirements on this guide. Send only current insurance, not historical insurance.
note: The new narrative does not mention IN1; the profiles still carry the segment.
recommendation: If IN1 stays in the profiles, say in the narrative that only current insurance is sent.

r15: Multiple names are allowed, but the legal name must be sent in the first repetition.
note: The requirement that L be first is retired and order is not enforced; NK1-2.7 SHALL be populated and the L name SHOULD be used when known. The address and phone repetition rules for NK1-4 to NK1-6 follow PID-11 and PID-13 (r15-f-pid-02, r15-f-pid-03).

r15: Set IDs number OBX segments across the message, but restarting at 1 in each order group is also allowed.
note: Both patterns remain allowed, and systems SHALL now accept either and SHALL NOT use OBX-1 for meaning. (The profiles' IZ-20 still reads as message-wide numbering.)

r15: LOINC is the standard when an appropriate code exists. With a local coding system, also send the local code; when no LOINC exists, the local code may be the only one. Either triplet may carry LOINC. The 2.3.1 practice of suffixing LOINC codes to group observations is no longer acceptable; use OBX-4.
note: OBX-3 SHALL now contain a LOINC code from the guide's subset; a local-only observation code is no longer allowed. Grouping with OBX-4 is kept.

section: ORC-2 and ORC-3 Placer and Filler Order Numbers
r15: ORC-3 is the sending system's unique ID for the immunization, which the receiver must store to support updates and deletes. For a historical immunization the sender SHALL still assign an ID, as if it had given the dose; for a dose not given (for example a refusal) it is 9999.
note: The role of ORC-3 is kept and extended to query responses (return the source's ORC-3 when known), and 9999 for refusals is kept. The rule that historical doses also get a sender-assigned ID is not stated, though the update and delete rules depend on it.
recommendation: State in 4.6.3 that the submitting system assigns ORC-3 to historical records as well.

r15: ORC-28 can flag special privacy rules for the vaccination in this order group (for example, state rules for HPV records), with R for restricted. A value records the patient's active choice; empty means no choice was made. Local guides describe its use.
note: Privacy is handled at the patient level (PD1-12). The new guide has no per-vaccination confidentiality; the field remains optional in the profiles.
recommendation: Either describe ORC-28 alongside PD1-12 in 4.5.6, or say that per-vaccination confidentiality is out of scope.

r15: The first repetition shall contain the legal name, with name type L.
note: The legal (official registry) name SHOULD be first, but receivers SHALL accept it in any repetition, and senders SHOULD NOT send an empty first repetition when there is no legal name.

r15: The primary mailing address must be first; if it is not sent, the first repetition is left empty. The patient's address belongs in PID-11 and may also be sent in NK1 with relationship Self.
note: Position no longer matters: the IIS SHALL read the address type in PID-11.7, and the first-repetition rule is retired. An IIS SHALL NOT require a Self NK1 that repeats PID-11. Birth state as a BDL address is pass 1 item r15-b-13.

r15: The first repetition is the primary number; if it is not sent, the first repetition is empty. Each kind of contact (for example a phone and an email) has its own repetition.
The primary care facility chosen at enrollment in an HMO plan; it is not the primary care practitioner or medical home, and its meaning should not be expanded to include the medical home.
note: The new guide does not mention PD1-3. It is optional in the profiles, so the caution matters little.

r15: In immunization messages, the publicity code is how the person wishes to be contacted for reminder and recall.
note: The data model lists a reminder/recall status for the patient, but the narrative does not say that PD1-11 carries it.
recommendation: Name PD1-11 as the field for the reminder/recall preference, for example in 2.3.2.1 or 4.5.

r15: Y means protect, N means sharing is fine, and empty means no determination; the state must be actively determined, or the field is empty. The earlier guide reversed Y; messages based on 2.3.1 or 2.4 keep the old meaning.
note: The new guide adds that IIS SHALL NOT require a default and apply jurisdiction rules after receipt. It does not repeat that 2.3.1 and 2.4 messages keep the old meaning; it says the reversal happened before 2.5.

r15: The status of the patient relative to the system creating the message. A provider may report the patient inactive while the IIS, in its own messages, reports the same patient active in the jurisdiction.
note: The provider-relative meaning is kept for submissions, but jurisdictional or IIS-derived statuses SHALL NOT be sent in HL7 messages, so an IIS no longer reports its own view of the patient in a response.

r15: ERR-5 is CWE with two triplets: one is reserved for table 0533 values, and the other may carry a more granular but equivalent local code.
note: ERR-5 now uses the national ERR-5 code set, with priorities for which codes an IIS SHALL implement. Locally invented codes are discouraged: a missing concept should be added to the national set instead. A local code in the second triplet is not mentioned.

section: QPD Input Parameter Field Description and Commentary (Z34 and Z44)
r15: For each query parameter, what happens when it is empty: the patient identifier is ignored without its assigning authority and type; a name without family or given name is treated as empty (name is required, so the query errors); empty middle name, suffix, or sex match anything; a birth date less precise than a day is ignored; an address without city or state is treated as empty, and an empty address type defaults to L; phone, mother's maiden name, multiple birth, birth order, and last update are ignored when empty. The guide does not specify the search method; systems should document their expectations.
note: The field-by-field rules are gone. Querying systems SHALL send all known information and the IIS SHALL use all of it, SHOULD use probabilistic or other advanced matching, and SHOULD document how identifiers are used. Partial values (for example a birth date to the month) are no longer defined.

r15: String data is printable ASCII (decimal 32 to 126), with no leading blanks. The only escape sequences allowed are those for the message delimiters.
note: The new guide requires support for 18 accented Latin characters in names (preserved or transliterated), and an IIS SHALL NOT reject a message because of them. That goes beyond printable ASCII. The escape-sequence limit is not repeated.
recommendation: Say which character encoding carries the accented characters (MSH-18 is not discussed), and whether the delimiter-only escape rule still holds.

r15: The use of OIDs in HD fields is encouraged; either the namespace ID (HD.1) or the universal ID (HD.2, an OID) is required.
note: For organization fields (MSH-4, MSH-22, RXA-11.4) the new guide standardizes on an IIS-defined identifier in HD.1; OIDs and other national identifiers are left for the future, not encouraged.

r15: The alternate identifier should be the closest match to the first. The order of the two triplets is not specified; the first triplet is no longer reserved for CVX in RXA-5.
note: The new guide requires IIS to accept CVX or NDC alone and to check that the two agree when both are sent, but does not say that either code may be in either triplet.
recommendation: State in 4.6.2.4 that CVX and NDC may appear in either CE triplet of RXA-5 and receivers check both.
